BEFORE WORK BEGINS

A proposal should
answer the practical questions.

Pricing is specific to the scope. Advertising spend, paid tools and other external costs are identified separately where relevant.

The work

Which deliverables, channels and review rounds are included?

The responsibilities

Who provides content, approves work and manages account access?

The checkpoints

Which milestones, dependencies and reporting dates guide delivery?

The handover

Who owns accounts and assets, and what support follows launch?

USEFUL REPORTING

More than a list
of activity.

01

What happened

The agreed activity and measures, with clear definitions.

02

What it means

Context, known limitations and feedback from the business.

03

What comes next

A prioritised recommendation, with decisions and inputs identified.

WORKING QUESTIONS

Clarity before
commitment.

Do you publish fixed packages?+

The website explains engagement types rather than fixed-price packages. A proposal follows a review of your requirements, existing assets and delivery needs.

Can our internal team stay involved?+

Yes. Review contacts, access, content responsibilities and handover requirements are agreed so the work fits your team.

What happens if the scope changes?+

Changes to deliverables, dependencies or priorities are reviewed before additional work is committed. Any fee or timing impact should be agreed.

Will we receive account access and files?+

Account ownership, working files, final formats, licensing and handover requirements are clarified in the proposal.
